# Node.js Guidelines
https://nodejs.org/en

## Purpose
Rules for writing and reviewing server-side, CLI and tooling code that runs on Node.js. Targets:
- **Node.js 24 (Active LTS)** — current production baseline.
- **Node.js 26** — Current line, promoted to **Active LTS on 28 October 2026**; use it for new projects that go live after that date and add it to the CI matrix now.

Never target end-of-life versions; Node 22 is in maintenance only. From Node 27 (2027) on, every major release becomes LTS (one release per year), so don't skip odd versions by habit.

**TypeScript rules apply:** for `.ts`/`.mts`/`.cts` files also follow [typescript.instructions.md](./typescript.instructions.md). This file adds Node-specific rules; where both cover the same topic, this file wins for runtime and platform questions.

## Project setup
- Declare the supported runtime in `package.json` (`"engines": { "node": ">=24" }`) and pin the exact version for development in `.nvmrc` / `.node-version` or the Dev Container.
- Node version manager: if the project already uses one (e.g. nvm, Volta via `"volta"` in `package.json`, asdf/mise via `.tool-versions` / `mise.toml`, n), keep using it. Otherwise use **fnm** as the default: pin the version in `.node-version`, and use `fnm use` / `fnm install` (enable `--use-on-cd` in the shell setup). Never mix managers in one project — no second version file, config or instructions for another manager.
- Use ES modules: `"type": "module"` in `package.json`; `.cjs` only for files that must be CommonJS. Use `import.meta.dirname` / `import.meta.filename` instead of `__dirname` / `__filename`.
- Define entry points and public API with the `"exports"` field (and `"imports"` with `#` aliases for internal paths); don't rely on deep imports.
- Import built-ins with the `node:` prefix (`import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";`).
- Package manager: npm, or pnpm/Yarn installed explicitly. Don't rely on Corepack being bundled (it's no longer shipped with newer Node releases). Commit the lock file and install with `npm ci` (or the equivalent) in CI.
- Scripts in `package.json` for `dev`, `build`, `start`, `test`, `lint`, `format`, `typecheck`.

## Use built-in features before adding dependencies
- Type stripping: run TypeScript files directly with `node file.ts` for scripts and tooling (erasable syntax only — no `enum`, `namespace` or parameter properties; see the TypeScript instructions). Still type-check with `tsc --noEmit` in CI.
- `node --env-file=.env` / `--env-file-if-exists` instead of `dotenv`.
- `node --watch` instead of `nodemon` for development.
- `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` (with `--test`, coverage via `--experimental-test-coverage` or the stable flag of the version in use) for libraries and tools; Vitest is fine for app projects that already use it.
- Global `fetch`, `WebSocket`, `AbortController`, `structuredClone`, `crypto.randomUUID()` and Web Streams instead of `node-fetch`, `ws` (client), `uuid` etc.
- `util.parseArgs` for simple CLIs, `util.styleText` for colored output, `fs.glob` for file globbing, `node:sqlite` for embedded SQLite.
- `Temporal` for dates and times on Node 26+; on Node 24 use `Date` only for timestamps and a well-maintained library for calendar logic.

## Async code and errors
- `async`/`await` everywhere; use the promise-based APIs (`node:fs/promises`, `node:timers/promises`, `node:stream/promises`). No callback-style APIs in new code, no `util.promisify` for APIs that already have promise versions.
- Never leave a promise unhandled: `await` it or handle it explicitly. The process crashes on unhandled rejections — keep it that way.
- Run independent work in parallel with `Promise.all` / `Promise.allSettled`, with bounded concurrency for large batches.
- Pass `AbortSignal` through all cancellable operations (`fetch`, timers, streams, your own APIs); use `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` for timeouts.
- Throw `Error` subclasses with `cause` (`new AppError("...", { cause: err })`); never throw strings.
- Handle `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` only to log and exit — never to keep running in an unknown state.
- Never block the event loop: no `*Sync` APIs in request paths, no CPU-heavy loops. Move CPU work to `worker_threads` or a separate process.

## Streams and I/O
- Use `pipeline()` from `node:stream/promises` to connect streams (handles errors and cleanup); never `.pipe()` without error handling.
- Stream large files and responses instead of loading them fully into memory.
- Build file paths with `node:path` (`path.join`, `path.resolve`) and `import.meta.dirname`; validate user-supplied paths stay inside the allowed directory.

## Configuration
- Read configuration from environment variables once at startup, validate it with a schema, and export a typed, frozen config object. Fail fast on missing or invalid values.
- Never commit `.env` files; provide `.env.example`.
- Set `NODE_ENV=production` in production.

## HTTP services
- Use [Fastify](https://fastify.dev) framework rather than raw `node:http` for services if no other framework is specified.
- Validate every request body, query and header with a schema; return consistent error responses (RFC 9457 problem details) and never leak stack traces.
- Graceful shutdown: on `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` stop accepting connections, finish in-flight requests with a timeout, close database pools, then exit.
- Health (`/healthz`) and readiness endpoints; structured JSON logging (e.g. Pino) with request IDs; OpenTelemetry for traces and metrics.
- Set timeouts (`server.requestTimeout`, `headersTimeout`, `keepAliveTimeout`) and body size limits.

## Serving Web Pages
- Use [AlpineJS](https://alpinejs.dev) as the preferred front end in combination with Fastify.
- Follow [alpinejs.instructions.md](./alpinejs.instructions.md).

## Security
- Never pass untrusted input to `child_process.exec`, `eval`, `new Function`, `vm` or dynamic `import()`; use `execFile`/`spawn` with argument arrays.
- Use parameterized queries for databases; never build SQL or shell commands with string concatenation.
- Protect against prototype pollution: don't merge untrusted objects into plain objects; use `Object.create(null)` or `Map` for dictionaries built from user input.
- Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for secret comparison, `crypto.scrypt`/Argon2 for passwords, `crypto.randomBytes` for tokens.
- Consider the permission model (`--permission` with `--allow-fs-read`, `--allow-fs-write`, `--allow-net` etc.) for scripts and services that process untrusted input.
- Keep dependencies minimal and current: `npm audit` / Dependabot, lock files, `npm ci --ignore-scripts` in CI where possible, and review new dependencies (maintenance, downloads, license, install scripts).
- Run containers as a non-root user; never run `npm install` in production images (install in a build stage).

## Performance
- Reuse HTTP connections (global `fetch` uses a keep-alive agent), database pools and clients; create them once.
- Cache expensive results; avoid synchronous JSON parsing of very large payloads on the main thread.
- Profile with `node --cpu-prof`, `--heap-prof` or `--inspect` before optimizing.

## Testing
- Unit tests colocated or in `test/`, run with `node --test` or Vitest; integration tests against real dependencies in containers (Testcontainers).
- Use `mock.timers` / fake timers instead of real delays; `t.mock` for module and function mocks.
- Test on every supported Node version in CI (currently 24 and 26).

## Code review focus
Flag in this order: command or SQL injection and `eval`, unhandled promises or swallowed errors, synchronous or CPU-heavy work on the event loop, missing input validation, secrets in code or logs, `.pipe()` without error handling, missing graceful shutdown, new dependencies that duplicate built-in features, CommonJS in new code, missing `node:` prefixes, unsupported Node versions.
